title: Power Automate Process Mining: analyse processes with object-centric process mining
summary: The briefing's rollout, licensing, prerequisites and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections should name the allocation API's request-body properties, cite the Fabric administrator role source and reconcile the governance checklist with the controls table.

claims.claim: OCPM analyses processes by following business objects rather than forcing each event into one case ID.
claims.quote: Object-centric process mining (OCPM) analyzes processes by following the real objects that interact—such as orders, deliveries, invoices, and payments—rather than forcing every event into a single case ID.

claims.claim: OCPM records events related to multiple objects and object types in one process.
claims.quote: OCPM models that reality by recording events that relate to many objects and object types in one process, preserving their relationships end-to-end.

claims.claim: The ingestion page describes storing the object-centric event log as CSV in Azure Data Lake Gen2 or OneLake.
claims.quote: Then, store the resulting file in a CSV format in either Azure Data Lake Gen2 or OneLake.

claims.claim: The maker begins at Process mining > Start here > Object-centric process mining.
claims.quote: On the navigation pane to the left, select Process mining > Start here. Select Object-centric process mining.

claims.claim: Mapping requires one Activity attribute.
claims.quote: You must map one attribute of type Activity.

claims.claim: Mapping requires one Start event attribute.
claims.quote: You must map one attribute of type Start event.

claims.claim: Mapping requires at least two Object type attributes.
claims.quote: You must map at least two attributes of type Object type.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The ingestion wizard's Choose where to export step offers Continue for Fabric export or Skip export.
claims.quote: In the Choose where to export step, select Continue to set up the export of OCPM semantic model in your Fabric workspace, or Skip export.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; What's changing
claims.claim: The maker selects the Fabric workspace and lakehouse for the optional export.
claims.quote: Select from the list of available Fabric workspaces. Select a Fabric Lakehouse in the workspace.

claims.claim: Export creates a semantic model and a report in Fabric.
claims.quote: When you publish a process to Fabric workspace, it creates a new DirectLake semantic model and an empty Power BI report connected to the semantic model.

claims.claim: After ingestion finishes, Process overview is the active tab.
claims.quote: After the ingestion finishes, you're navigated to the process intelligence experience for OCPM with the Process overview tab active.

claims.claim: Process overview includes a process map.
claims.quote: The Process Map is a central visualization showing the process flow across multiple objects

claims.claim: Process overview includes object counts.
claims.quote: Objects Count is a donut chart that summarizes the distribution of all objects in the event log.

claims.claim: Process overview includes a process analysis widget.
claims.quote: Process analysis provides detailed statistical analysis based on the leading object and an optional path

claims.claim: Filters refine the Process overview analytics.
claims.quote: All visuals in the Process overview react to the selected filter criteria.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Environment makers can create, share and contribute to processes.
claims.quote: The Environment maker role can use the process mining capabilities to create, share, and contribute to processes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Object-centric event logs carry object IDs.
claims.quote: In OCPM, you work with object-centric event data where each row is an event (with activity and timestamp) and has one or more columns listing the object IDs per object type that the event touched

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Event and object attributes, including financial attributes, are optional but highly recommended.
claims.quote: Event and Object level attributes (including financial) are optional but highly recommended for more detailed analysis

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: The exported model's access is governed by Fabric permissions.
claims.quote: Workspace roles are used to control access to workspaces and the content within them. A Fabric administrator can assign workspace roles to individual users or groups.

claims.claim: Stored process data uses mostly Dataverse file capacity.
claims.quote: Depending on the size of the process data you import, you might run out of Dataverse storage capacity. The process data we store uses mostly file capacity.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Dataverse security roles govern access to process mining features.
claims.quote: The process mining capability relies on environment security and Microsoft Dataverse security roles and privileges to grant access to its features in Power Automate.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators and system customizers can access all processes in the environment.
claims.quote: Administrators and system customizers can access all processes created in the environment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Process Mining User role can only view process reports.
claims.quote: The Process Mining User security role can only view created process reports.

claims.claim: OneLake ingestion requires sharing the Fabric workspace with the Process Insight Prod service principal as Admin.
claims.quote: The Fabric workspace needs to be shared to the Process Insight Prod service principal with an Admin role.

claims.claim: The user performing the initial Fabric workspace setup for the environment needs the Admin role.
claims.quote: The Admin role must be attributed to the user performing the initial workspace setup for the environment for the other users in the same environment.

claims.claim: The OCPM documentation describes analytics and export, not autonomous business actions.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate object centric process mining overview ingest event log licensing security; read object-centric-overview, object-centric-ingest-event-log, object-centric-process-overview and object-centric-semantic-model. These describe ingestion, analytics, refresh and export.

claims.claim: Refresh Data triggers full ingestion and creation of the process model.
claims.quote: Refresh Data: Button to reload and refresh the displayed analytics with the most recent data (this action triggers the full ingestion and creation of the process model).

claims.where: controls[1]; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No OCPM-specific on/off switch is documented in the admin UI or API as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate object-centric process mining admin enable disable switch Power Platform API Dataverse table; "object-centric" "disable"; "object-centric" "production-ready". Read OCPM overview, ingest and process overview; settings-features search documents only a general preview switch.

claims.claim: Mixed licensing describes per-user Power Automate Premium capacity and the tenant-wide Process Mining add-on.
claims.quote: The Power Automate Premium license is a per-user license with the following offerings: ... The Process Mining add-on is a tenant-wide license that's available for the Power Automate Premium license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Process mining is licensed as part of Microsoft Power Automate.
claims.quote: Process mining is licensed as part of Microsoft Power Automate.

claims.claim: Each Power Automate Premium licence contributes 50 MB of process mining capacity to the tenant-wide pool.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.

claims.claim: Premium's pooled contribution is limited to 100 GB per tenant.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.

claims.claim: At 100 GB, processing more data requires purchasing the Process Mining add-on.
claims.quote: When you reach 100 GB, you need to purchase the Power Automate Process Mining add-on to process more data.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: The Process Mining add-on is tenant-wide and requires Power Automate Premium.
claims.quote: Required prerequisite: Power Automate Premium. Multiple add-ons can be applied to a single prerequisite.

claims.claim: The add-on adds 100 GB of process mining capacity.
claims.quote: An extra 100 GB of process mining capacity to the capacity pool, which users with the Power Automate Premium license can use.

claims.claim: The add-on includes an extra 2 GB of Dataverse database capacity.
claims.quote: An extra 2 GB of Dataverse database capacity.

claims.claim: The add-on includes an extra 1 TB of Dataverse file capacity.
claims.quote: An extra 1 TB of Dataverse file capacity.

claims.claim: The licensing FAQ lists the Process Mining add-on at USD $5,000 for 100 GB of data stored per month.
claims.quote: List Price (USD): $5,000 for 100 GB of data stored/month

claims.claim: Microsoft says to purchase capacity for peak utilisation over a 12-month contract.
claims.quote: Capacity should be purchased for the peak utilization over a 12-month contract period.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Customers can assess their highest monthly process mining usage in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Yes, customers can assess their highest monthly Process Mining usage to understand capacity needed. Current and past usage data are available in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Power BI licences are not included in Power Automate Process Mining.
claims.quote: Power BI licenses aren't included in Power Automate Process Mining.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The OCPM pages name no separate OCPM-specific licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate object-centric process mining licensing price meter. Read OCPM overview, ingest, process overview and semantic model; process-advisor-overview licensing and Power Platform licensing FAQs publish the product's licences, not a separate OCPM licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate OCPM-specific meter is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate object-centric process mining licensing price meter. Read OCPM overview, ingest, process overview, semantic model, process-advisor-overview and licensing FAQs; search returned pay-as-you-go flow-run meters, not an OCPM-specific meter.

claims.where: summary; Cost and licensing; Why it matters
claims.claim: OCPM belongs to Power Automate Process Mining and uses its published process mining capacity entitlement.
claims.quote: Process mining is licensed as part of Microsoft Power Automate. Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.

claims.claim: Fabric export creates the semantic model on Fabric Lakehouse delta tables.
claims.quote: The semantic model is created on top of Fabric Lakehouse delta tables.

claims.claim: OneLake lakehouse storage is billed pay-as-you-go per GB.
claims.quote: OneLake storage is billed at a pay-as-you-go rate per GB of data used and doesn't consume Fabric Capacity Units (CUs). Fabric items like lakehouses and warehouses consume OneLake storage.

claims.claim: OneLake read and write requests consume Fabric Capacity Units.
claims.quote: Requests to OneLake, such as reading or writing data, consume Fabric Capacity Units.

claims.claim: Process mining requires a Power Platform environment with a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: A Microsoft Power Platform environment with a Microsoft Dataverse database.

claims.claim: OneLake ingestion requires a Fabric workspace other than My workspace.
claims.quote: A Fabric workspace that's different from the default My workspace.

claims.claim: OneLake ingestion requires the setting allowing external apps to access OneLake data to be on.
claims.quote: Ensure that Users can access data stored in OneLake with apps external to the Fabric option is switched on in the OneLake tenant settings.

claims.claim: OneLake ingestion offers no post-ingestion data transformation.
claims.quote: No data transformation is available post ingestion.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The general add-on allocation page is reached in Power Platform admin center at Licensing > Capacity add-ons > Summary > Add-ons > Manage.
claims.quote: On the navigation pane, select Licensing. In the Licensing pane, select Capacity add-ons. On the Capacity page, select the Summary tab. ... Scroll down to the Add-ons section, and select Manage.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The cited tutorial documents PATCH of the environment allocations endpoint with api-version=2022-03-01-preview to adjust add-on allocations.
claims.quote: Invoke-RestMethod -Method Patch -Uri "https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/environments/$EnvironmentId/allocations?api-version=2022-03-01-preview"
claims.fix: Append to controls[0].note: 'The request body sets currencyAllocations, with currencyType and allocated specifying each allocation.' These properties appear in the cited tutorial's request body. Keep the existing distinction between the tutorial's API version and the current reference.

claims.claim: The current Currency Allocation reference lists ProcessMiningDataStorage as an allocatable currency type.
claims.quote: ExternalCurrencyType ... The available currency type that can be allocated to an environment. ... ProcessMiningDataStorage

claims.claim: The generic capacity add-on UI page does not explicitly identify the Process Mining add-on.
claims.quote: Searched: Process Mining and ProcessMiningDataStorage in the fetched capacity-add-on page. Its allocation examples identify app passes, flow per business process and portal page views, not Process Mining.

claims.claim: The tutorial uses version 2022-03-01-preview, whereas the current Currency Allocation reference documents 2024-10-01.
claims.quote: API Version: 2024-10-01. PATCH https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/environments/{environmentId}/allocations?api-version=2024-10-01

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to assign the internal Process Mining Application role to users.
claims.quote: The Process Mining Application is an internal security role that process mining uses. ... Don't assign this security role to users.

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to modify the privileges of Process Mining User or Process Mining Application.
claims.quote: Don't modify the set of privileges in the Process Mining User or Process Mining Application security roles.

claims.claim: A Fabric administrator can configure the OneLake tenant setting in Fabric.
claims.quote: These roles provide access to the admin experience in Govern and control over organization-wide Fabric settings, usage metrics, and admin features, except for licensing.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/admin/roles to sources for the Fabric administrator statement; retain the existing OneLake tenant-settings citation.

claims.claim: OCPM-specific audit events for process creation, ingestion and sharing are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate object-centric process mining audit logging creation ingestion sharing; "object-centric" "audit" "Power Automate"; "process mining" "audit logs". Read OCPM pages, Dataverse auditing and compliance/privacy search excerpts; no OCPM-specific events identified.

claims.claim: The first controls row represents the checklist's capacity-usage monitoring control.
claims.quote: Review capacity usage in the Power Platform admin center against the licensed pool (first controls row). / Process mining capacity add-on allocated to an environment
claims.fix: Remove '(first controls row)' from the After rollout usage-monitoring bullet: that row allocates capacity rather than displaying process mining usage. The checklist names capacity-usage monitoring without a corresponding row; do not add a row as part of this correction.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The controls table covers the checklist's optional Fabric export decision.
claims.quote: Agree whether makers should use the optional Choose where to export step or Skip export / The controls table lists only capacity allocation and the undocumented OCPM on/off switch.
claims.fix: The At rollout export-decision bullet names a control with no table row. Remove that checklist bullet if table/checklist parity is required; retain the supported export description in What's changing. Do not add a control row as part of this correction.

claims.claim: OneLake source data must already be in final event log format before ingestion.
claims.quote: All data must be in final event log format and meet the requirements listed in Data requirements. Data should be ready to be mapped to the process mining schema.
